options: A) To show that useful language practice can be built into ordinary routines
B) To show that learners need to make major changes to their daily lives to improve

A.text: When my city council proposed to transform an old industrial site into a community garden, I was excited. Initially, I was skeptical about the project's feasibility, given the site's historical contamination. However, after thorough soil treatments and planning, we successfully created a vibrant space. It took teamwork and dedication, but seeing local residents coming together to enjoy the green urban oasis is rewarding. The positive effects on our mental health and community spirit are undeniable. Since then, I've been advocating for additional green projects to enhance urban living. Although some challenges remain, the benefits of having green spaces close to home make it worthwhile. We've also noticed how the garden has made the area feel cleaner and more pleasant. Despite some opposition, particularly from motorists who lost parking spaces, overall, the initiative has been embraced warmly.

B.text: A few years ago, I initiated a rooftop garden project on top of the commercial building where I work. The primary goal was to reduce the building's energy use and carbon footprint by improving insulation. Initially, raising awareness and funding were challenging, but persistence paid off. The garden now boasts a range of plants that not only beautify the space but also benefit the environment. Colleagues have embraced the opportunity to unwind in the tranquil setting during breaks. Furthermore, it's sparked a noticeable shift in attitudes towards environmental responsibility among staff. There's now a growing interest in expanding similar projects throughout the city. Despite lacking expertise initially, I've learned a lot about sustainable practices. The transformation has been remarkable, and I'm proud to have led this initiative, proving that even small changes can lead to significant impacts.
